### Introduction:

This time you will create a data again

Special thanks to [Chris Albon](http://chrisalbon.com/) for sharing the dataset and materials.
All the credits to this exercise belongs to him.

In order to understand about it go to [here](https://blog.codinghorror.com/a-visual-explanation-of-sql-joins/).

### Step 1. Import the necessary libraries

```{r step1, message=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
```

### Step 2. Create the 3 DataFrames based on the following raw data

```{r given-data}
raw_data_1 <- list(
  subject_id = c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5"),
  first_name = c("Alex", "Amy", "Allen", "Alice", "Ayoung"),
  last_name = c("Anderson", "Ackerman", "Ali", "Aoni", "Atiches"))

raw_data_2 <- list(
  subject_id = c("4", "5", "6", "7", "8"),
  first_name = c("Billy", "Brian", "Bran", "Bryce", "Betty"),
  last_name = c("Bonder", "Black", "Balwner", "Brice", "Btisan"))

raw_data_3 <- list(
  subject_id = c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "7", "8", "9", "10", "11"),
  test_id = c(51, 15, 15, 61, 16, 14, 15, 1, 61, 16))
```

### Step 3. Assign each to a variable called data1, data2, data3

```{r}
data1 <- as_tibble(raw_data_1)
data2 <- as_tibble(raw_data_2)
data3 <- as_tibble(raw_data_3)

data3
```

### Step 4. Join the two dataframes along rows and assign all_data

```{r}
all_data <- bind_rows(data1, data2)
all_data
```

### Step 5. Join the two dataframes along columns and assign to all_data_col

```{r}
# a tibble can't have repeated column names, so bind_cols() renames them
all_data_col <- bind_cols(data1, data2, .name_repair = "unique")
all_data_col
```

### Step 6. Print data3

```{r}
data3
```

### Step 7. Merge all_data and data3 along the subject_id value

```{r}
inner_join(all_data, data3, by = "subject_id")
```

### Step 8. Merge only the data that has the same 'subject_id' on both data1 and data2

```{r}
inner_join(data1, data2, by = "subject_id")
```

### Step 9. Merge all values in data1 and data2, with matching records from both sides where available.

```{r}
full_join(data1, data2, by = "subject_id")
```
